title: UK asylum AI: documented roles and disclosure limits

rows.name: Asylum Case Summarisation
rows.value: AI summarises interview transcripts for caseworkers
rows.notes: Role in a small-scale pilot, not automated grant or refusal. Later ministerial correspondence says both tools operational.

rows.name: Asylum Policy Search
rows.value: AI finds and summarises country policy information
rows.notes: Role in a pilot; policy-search assistance is not itself an eligibility decision.

rows.name: Applicant notification
rows.value: Applicants not specifically told AI was used in their claim
rows.notes: Ministerial statement at a specific date. Does not establish absence of every route of appeal.

rows.name: Independent audit
rows.value: No independent audit planned at that stage
rows.sourceLocator: Page 2, first paragraph under continued Oversight and Audit
rows.notes: Dated ministerial statement, not a claim that audits can never occur. Internal testing is distinct from independent audit.

coverage.population: Two Home Office AI tool roles and two dated official oversight statements, 2024–2026
coverage.included: 4 populated records; Two Home Office AI tool roles and two dated official oversight statements, 2024–2026
coverage.omitted: All asylum systems globally, final eligibility automation, individual case accuracy, legal conclusions and complete appeal routes
coverage.missingness: Unlisted entities are missing, not zero.

uncertainty: Government descriptions and disclosed ministerial correspondence, not an independent system audit. NGO investigation disputes aspects of quality assurance. The source states humans decide cases; AI assistance can still affect the information they see. June and August statements must not be collapsed into an undated current policy.
